data.one_liner: Library for working with OpenID Connect and implementing clients in Dart.
data.what_it_does: Discovers OpenID Provider metadata, parses and validates ID tokens, and provides tools for implementing implicit and authorization code flows.
use_when: You need to authenticate users via OpenID Connect or OAuth2 providers.
You are building a client for command line, web, or mobile applications using OIDC.
avoid_when: You exclusively want pre-built platform-native sign-in flows like Firebase Auth or Google Sign-In widgets.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Implements discovery, ID token validation, and RP initiated logout.
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration for non-standard OAuth2 providers.
data.setup_notes: Requires defining redirect URIs and setting up the appropriate authentication client for your target platform (IO, browser, etc.).

alternatives.name: google_sign_in
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need native Google sign-in integration.

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your backend and user management are handled by Firebase.
